gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in Anker's E10 + Power Dock system, a third-party portable generator can't use the E10 AC Generator Adapter (Anker: 'Currently not compatible with Power Dock'). Battery-level auto-start then needs either Anker's Smart Generator 5500 on its own power-and-communication DC cable (up to 4,500 W) or a 240 V standby generator with Two Wire or Utility Sensing control, a 24 kW surge limit and the May 2026 firmware.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited FranklinWH pages: the support article 'Can I use a generator with my FranklinWH system?', the Generator Module accessory page and the aPower 2 page. The support article only says portable or standby generators connect through the aGate generator module or aHub, and to match the generator's watts to the essential loads. It gives no kW limit, no start-wire type, no voltage and no firmware. The Generator Module page says it works with 'a range of both standby and portable generators' and gives no limits. None of them covers an Anker or any other kit sold as one cart, and none names an adapter that a given hub can't use. This finding decides which generator path belongs in the set.
kit_items: Battery + inverter: Anker SOLIX E10 Power Module with B6000 battery modules (6.144 kWh each). It is the only battery that takes the Smart Generator 5500's DC cable, which carries power and communication.

Transfer hub: Anker SOLIX Power Dock (≤20 ms switchover). Choose it over the Smart Inlet Box for standby-generator auto start, which Anker says is 'exclusively available for the E10 + Power Dock setup'. It must be installed by an electrician.

Generator: Anker SOLIX Smart Generator 5500 (Tri-Fuel: gasoline, LPG, natural gas). It joins the E10 through DC coupling with 'Auto Start by SOC'. Anker says it is not compatible with Anker SOLIX X1, and quiet mode works only when paired with the E10.
Leave out: E10 AC Generator Adapter. Anker says it is 'Currently not compatible with Power Dock' and works only with E10 Standalone or Smart Inlet Box setups.

Alternative to the Smart Generator 5500 (not in this cart): your own 240 V standby generator wired to the Power Dock. It must support Two Wire or Utility Sensing control, stay at or under 24 kW surge, and needs the May 2026 E10 + Power Dock firmware.

items: Anker SOLIX E10 (Power Module + 2× B6000 Battery) + Power Dock + Smart Generator 5500 | https://www.ankersolix.com/products/e10-power-module-2-battery-power-dock-smart-generator-5500 | $9,399.00 | 2026-11-13

A smaller bundle, E10 + Power Dock + Smart Generator 5500 with the B6000 sold as an option, was $7,399.00 at https://www.ankersolix.com/products/e10-power-dock-smart-generator-5500 (read 2026-11-13). storecheck.py returned HTTP 404 for this store, so both prices come from the opened product pages.

findings.product: Anker SOLIX E10 AC Generator Adapter
findings.label: Hub compatibility
findings.value: Compatible with E10 Standalone and Smart Inlet Box setups; not compatible with Power Dock
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX E10 AC Generator Adapter (add-on)
findings.note: Verbatim: 'Currently not compatible with Power Dock.' The page sends Power Dock owners to the Power Dock manual.

findings.product: Anker SOLIX E10 AC Generator Adapter
findings.label: Bypass rating
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX E10 AC Generator Adapter (add-on)
findings.note: Maker's product page. The page lists the cable as both 500 mm and 50 cm, which are the same length.

findings.label: Standby generator requirement
findings.value: 240 V standby generator supporting Two Wire or Utility Sensing control; max surge 24 kW; enabled by May 2026 firmware; E10 + Power Dock only
findings.source_title: E10 Standby Generator Integration: Setup and Features Guide (Anker, 2026-05-19)
findings.note: Verbatim: 'This feature is exclusively available for the E10 + Power Dock setup' and 'must support Two Wire or Utility Sensing control modes.' The generator starts at a user-set battery level and stops when the battery is full. The article gives no default threshold.

findings.label: Link to E10
findings.value: Dedicated cable carrying power and communication (DC coupling); up to 4,500 W DC; Auto Start by SOC
findings.note: Per the FAQ, DC output requires pairing with the E10. The starting-watt table reads 4,500 W gasoline, 4,500 W LPG and 4,000 W natural gas. The spec-table labels look misaligned, so I did not use them as the DC rating.

findings.label: Exclusions
findings.value: Not compatible with Anker SOLIX X1; one fuel at a time; outdoor use only; quiet mode only when paired with E10
findings.note: The FAQ also says AC coupling works with 'F3000, with more models planned'. The F3800 Plus is not named.

findings.label: AC output
findings.value: 3,600 W at 120 V, 60 Hz; outlets NEMA 5-20R ×1, TT-30R ×1
findings.note: The AC output is 120 V only. The page lists no 240 V outlet.

findings.product: Anker SOLIX E10 (Power Module + 2× Battery) + Power Dock + Smart Generator 5500
findings.label: Output and capacity
findings.value: 10 kW continuous with 2+ batteries (7.6 kW with one); 2 × 6.144 kWh = 12.29 kWh; expandable 6–90 kWh; one Power Dock takes up to 3 E10 units
findings.source_title: E10 (Power Module + 2× Battery) + Power Dock + Smart Generator 5500
findings.note: Capacity is 2 × 6.144 kWh from the page's FAQ. The page also says neither the Power Dock nor the E10 can export to the grid.

findings.label: AC charge limit from a generator
findings.value: Up to 1,800 W on 120 V; up to 7,680 W on 240 V
findings.source_title: Automatic generator integration for a home battery (Anker, 2026-08-27, updated 2026-10-30)
findings.note: The same article says 'most portable models lack SOC-based or app-controlled auto-start', and that full DC plus communication automation is strongest with the Smart Generator 5500.

findings.label: Generator connection stated
findings.value: Generator connects to the aGate generator module option or the aHub dock; portable or standby
findings.source_title: Can I use a generator with my FranklinWH system?
findings.note: Baseline for the comparison. No kW limit, start-wire type, voltage or firmware is given.
